title.zh: 卷四十五 列傳第三十九 王僧辯
title.raw: 卷四十五 列傳第三十九 王僧辯 Volume 45: Wang Sengbian

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第四十五 列傳第三十九

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 45, Biography 39
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 45, Biography 39

sentences.zh: 王僧辯

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian

sentences.zh: 王僧辯字君才，右衛將軍神念之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Sengbian, courtesy name Juncai, was the son of Right Palace Guard General Wang Shennian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengbian, styled Juncai, was son of Right Palace Guard General Wang Shennian.

sentences.zh: 以天監中隨父來奔。

translations.literal: In the Heavenly Surveillance era he followed his father in coming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: During Heavenly Surveillance he came with his father to defect.

sentences.zh: 起家爲湘東王國左常侍。

translations.literal: His first office was Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Left Regular Attendant in Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王爲丹陽尹，轉府行參軍。

translations.literal: When the prince became governor of Danyang, he was transferred to acting staff aide in the prince's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became Danyang governor, he became acting staff aide.

sentences.zh: 王出守會稽，兼中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: When the prince went out to govern Kuaiji, he concurrently served as middle army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince governed Kuaiji, he served concurrently as middle army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 王爲荊州，仍除中兵，在限內。

translations.literal: When the prince took Jingzhou, he was again appointed middle army officer, within the term limit.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took Jingzhou, he was again made middle army officer within his term.

sentences.zh: 時武寧郡反，王命僧辯討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Wuning commandery rebelled; the prince ordered Sengbian to suppress and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuning commandery rebelled; the prince sent Sengbian to put it down.

sentences.zh: 遷貞威將軍、武寧太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Sincere Might and governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted General of Sincere Might and governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 尋遷振遠將軍、廣平太守。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to General Who Quells the Distance and governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became General Who Quells the Distance and governor of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，還爲王府中錄事，參軍如故。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned as chief clerk of the prince's headquarters, his staff officer post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned as the prince's chief clerk, still staff officer.

sentences.zh: 王被徵爲護軍，僧辯兼府司馬。

translations.literal: When the prince was summoned as Protector of the Army, Sengbian concurrently served as headquarters marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was summoned Protector of the Army, Sengbian served concurrently as headquarters marshal.

sentences.zh: 王爲江州，仍除雲騎將軍司馬，守湓城。

translations.literal: When the prince took Jiangzhou, he was again appointed marshal to the General of the Cloud Banner Cavalry and defended Tuncheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took Jiangzhou, he was again marshal to the Cloud Banner general and defended Tuncheng.

sentences.zh: 俄監安陸郡，無幾而還。

translations.literal: Shortly he supervised Anlu commandery, then before long returned.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly supervised Anlu, then soon returned.

sentences.zh: 尋爲新蔡太守，猶帶司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon after he became governor of Xincai, still holding the marshal post, his general rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became governor of Xincai, still marshal, same general rank.

sentences.zh: 王除荊州，爲貞毅將軍府諮議參軍事，賜食千人，代柳仲禮爲竟陵太守，改號雄信將軍。

translations.literal: When the prince took Jingzhou again, he was made staff adviser to the headquarters as General of Steadfast Resolution with a fief of one thousand, replacing Liu Zhongli as governor of Jingling, and his title was changed to General of Mighty Trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took Jingzhou again, he was staff adviser as General of Steadfast Resolution with a thousand-household fief, replacing Liu Zhongli at Jingling and retitled General of Mighty Trust.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景反，王命僧辯假節，總督舟師一萬，兼糧饋赴援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled the prince ordered Sengbian, with acting staff of authority, to command ten thousand river troops and concurrently transport grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled the prince gave Sengbian acting staff, command of ten thousand river troops, and grain transport for relief.

sentences.zh: 才至京都，宮城陷沒，天子蒙塵。

translations.literal: He had just reached the capital when the palace city fell and the Son of Heaven suffered dust.
translations.idiomatic: He had just reached the capital when the palace fell and the emperor was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 僧辯與柳仲禮兄弟及趙伯超等，先屈膝于景，然後入朝。

translations.literal: Sengbian, together with Liu Zhongli and his brothers and Zhao Bochao and others, first bent the knee to Jing and only then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian, with the Liu brothers and Zhao Bochao and others, first submitted to Jing, then entered court.

sentences.zh: 景悉收其軍實，而厚加綏撫。

translations.literal: Jing seized all their military stores yet treated them generously with soothing measures.
translations.idiomatic: Jing confiscated their stores yet soothed them generously.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣僧辯歸于竟陵，於是倍道兼行，西就世祖。

translations.literal: Before long he sent Sengbian back to Jingling; thereupon Sengbian traveled day and night by double stages west to join the Heir of Zhenhui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jing sent him back to Jingling; Sengbian then raced west by double stages to join the Heir of Zhenhui.

sentences.zh: 世祖承制，以僧辯爲領軍將軍。

translations.literal: The Heir, acting on imperial authority, appointed Sengbian General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir, acting on imperial authority, made Sengbian General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 及荊、湘疑貳，軍師失律，世祖又命僧辯及鮑泉統軍討之，分給兵糧，剋日就道。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang grew doubtful and the army lost discipline, the Heir again ordered Sengbian and Bao Quan to command troops to suppress them, allotting soldiers and grain with a fixed day to take the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang wavered and the army lost discipline, the Heir again ordered Sengbian and Bao Quan south with troops and grain, fixed to march on a set day.

sentences.zh: 時僧辨以竟陵部下猶未盡來，意欲待集，然後上頓。

translations.literal: At the time Sengbian's Jingling subordinates had not all arrived; he wished to wait until they gathered before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: His Jingling troops had not all arrived; he wished to wait until they gathered before marching.

sentences.zh: 謂鮑泉曰：「我與君俱受命南討，而軍容若此，計將安之？

translations.literal: He said to Bao Quan: "You and I were both ordered on a southern campaign, yet our army looks like this—what plan can settle it?
translations.idiomatic: He told Bao Quan, "We were both ordered south, yet our force looks like this—what are we to do?

sentences.zh: 」泉曰：「旣稟廟算，驅率驍勇，事等沃雪，何所多慮。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Having received the temple's battle plan, we drive fierce warriors—the affair is like pouring snow on boiling water; what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: " Quan said, "We have the court's plan and drive fierce men—the thing is like snow on boiling water; why so much worry?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Sengbian said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 君之所言故是，文士之常談耳。

translations.literal: What you say is indeed the usual talk of literary men.
translations.idiomatic: What you say is the usual talk of literary men.

sentences.zh: 河東少有武幹，兵刃又強，新破軍師，養銳待敵，自非精兵一萬，不足以制之。

translations.literal: East of the river has few men of military talent, and their weapons are strong; they have just broken our army and are sharpening their edge to await the enemy—unless we have ten thousand elite troops we cannot control them.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river has few soldiers of real talent and strong arms; they have just crushed our army and rest their blades—without ten thousand elites we cannot hold them.

sentences.zh: 我竟陵甲士，數經行陣，已遣召之，不久當及。

translations.literal: My Jingling armored men have marched the lines many times; I have already sent to summon them and they will arrive before long.
translations.idiomatic: My Jingling veterans have marched many campaigns; I have summoned them and they will come soon.

sentences.zh: 雖期日有限，猶可重申，欲與卿共入言之，望相佐也。

translations.literal: Though the deadline is limited, we can still ask for an extension; I wish to go in with you to speak—please lend me your support.
translations.idiomatic: Though the day is fixed, we can still ask for delay; I want to go in with you—stand with me.

sentences.zh: 」泉曰：「成敗之舉，繫此一行，遲速之宜，終當仰聽。

translations.literal: " Quan said: "Success or failure hangs on this one march; whether to hurry or delay must in the end be heard from above.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan said, "Success or failure rides on this march; fast or slow we must obey above.

sentences.zh: 」世祖性嚴忌，微聞其言，以爲遷延不肯去，稍已含怒。

translations.literal: The Heir was stern and suspicious by nature; he faintly heard their words and thought Sengbian was delaying and unwilling to go, and was already somewhat angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir was stern and suspicious; he caught wind of their talk, thought Sengbian was stalling, and was already angry.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯將入，謂泉曰：「我先發言，君可見係。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was about to enter he told Quan: "I will speak first; you may be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Before entering he told Quan, "I will speak first; you may be seized.

sentences.zh: 」泉又許之。

translations.literal: " Quan again promised.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan agreed again.

sentences.zh: 及見世祖，世祖迎問曰：「卿已辦乎？

translations.literal: When they saw the Heir he came forward asking: "Are you ready?
translations.idiomatic: When they saw the Heir he came forward asking, "Are you ready?

sentences.zh: 何日當發？

translations.literal: What day will you set out?
translations.idiomatic: What day do you march?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯具對，如向所言。

translations.literal: " Sengbian answered in full as he had said before.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian answered fully as before.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒，按劍厲聲曰：「卿憚行邪！

translations.literal: The Heir was greatly enraged; he gripped his sword and said in a harsh voice: "You fear the march!
translations.idiomatic: The Heir raged, gripped his sword, and shouted, "You fear the march!

sentences.zh: 」因起入內。

translations.literal: " He rose and went within.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose and went within.

sentences.zh: 泉震怖失色，竟不敢言。

translations.literal: Quan was shaken and turned pale, and in the end did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Quan shook with terror and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 須臾，遣左右數十人收僧辯。

translations.literal: Before long he sent several tens of attendants to seize Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he sent dozens of attendants to seize Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 旣至，謂曰：「卿拒命不行，是欲同賊，今唯有死耳。

translations.literal: When he arrived the Heir said to him: "You defy orders and will not go—you wish to join the rebels; now there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the Heir said, "You defy orders and refuse to march—you would join the rebels; now only death remains.

sentences.zh: 」僧辯對曰：「僧辯食祿旣深，憂責實重，今日就戮，豈敢懷恨。

translations.literal: Sengbian replied: "Sengbian has eaten salary deeply and bears heavy responsibility; coming to execution today, how could I harbor resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian replied, "I have eaten deep salary and bear heavy blame; facing execution today, how could I resent it?

sentences.zh: 但恨不見老母。

translations.literal: I only regret not seeing my old mother.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret not seeing my old mother.

sentences.zh: 」世祖因斫之，中其左髀，流血至地。

translations.literal: The Heir thereupon hacked at him, striking his left thigh; blood ran to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir hacked at him, cutting his left thigh; blood pooled on the ground.

sentences.zh: 僧辯悶絕，久之方蘇。

translations.literal: Sengbian lost consciousness and only after long time revived.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian fainted and only after long time revived.

sentences.zh: 卽送付廷尉，並收其子侄，並皆繫之。

translations.literal: He was at once sent to the Minister of Justice, and his sons and nephews were seized and all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent at once to the Minister of Justice; his sons and nephews were seized and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 會岳陽王軍襲江陵，人情搔擾，未知其備。

translations.literal: Just then the Prince of Yueyang's army raided Jiangling; the people were agitated and did not know his preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Prince of Yueyang raided Jiangling; the people were unsettled and did not know his plans.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣左右往獄，問計於僧辯，僧辯具陳方略，登卽赦爲城內都督。

translations.literal: The Heir sent an attendant to the prison to ask Sengbian's plan; Sengbian laid out his strategy in full and was immediately pardoned and made commander within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir sent an attendant to the prison for Sengbian's plan; he laid out his strategy and was immediately pardoned and made city commander.

sentences.zh: 俄而岳陽奔退，而鮑泉力不能剋長沙，世祖乃命僧辯代之。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Yueyang fled in defeat, and Bao Quan could not take Changsha by force; the Heir then ordered Sengbian to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yueyang fled in defeat and Quan could not take Changsha; the Heir ordered Sengbian to replace him.

sentences.zh: 數泉以十罪，遣舍人羅重歡領齋仗三百人，與僧辯俱發。

translations.literal: He charged Quan with ten crimes and sent the palace gentleman Luo Chonghuan leading three hundred armed guards with Sengbian to depart together.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Quan with ten crimes and sent palace gentleman Luo Chonghuan with three hundred armed guards to march with Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 旣至，遣通泉云：「羅舍人被令，送王竟陵來。

translations.literal: When they arrived he sent word to Quan: "Gentleman Luo has been ordered to deliver the Wang of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he sent word to Quan, "Gentleman Luo is ordered to deliver the Wang of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 」泉甚愕然，顧左右曰：「得王竟陵助我經略，賊不足平。

translations.literal: " Quan was greatly startled and said to those beside him: "With the Wang of Jingling to aid my strategy, the bandits cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan was startled and told his attendants, "With the Wang of Jingling to aid me, the rebels will not stand.

sentences.zh: 」俄而重歡齎令書先入，僧辯從齋仗繼進，泉方拂席，坐而待之。

translations.literal: Before long Chonghuan carried the written order in first and Sengbian followed with the armed guard; Quan had just brushed the mat and sat waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chonghuan entered with the written order and Sengbian followed with the guard; Quan had just brushed the mat and sat waiting.

sentences.zh: 僧辯旣入，背泉而坐，曰：「鮑郎，卿有罪，令旨使我鏁卿，勿以故意見待。

translations.literal: When Sengbian entered he sat with his back to Quan and said: "Master Bao, you have guilt; by imperial order I am to lock you—do not take it as old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian entered he sat with his back to Quan and said, "Master Bao, you are guilty; by order I lock you—do not take it as old friendship.

sentences.zh: 」因語重歡出令，泉卽下地，鏁于床側。

translations.literal: " He told Chonghuan to produce the order; Quan at once left the floor and was chained beside the bed.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Chonghuan produce the order; Quan left the floor and was chained beside the bed.

sentences.zh: 僧辯仍部分將帥，幷力攻圍，遂平湘土。

translations.literal: Sengbian then deployed the generals and joined forces in siege, and pacified the land of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian then deployed the generals, joined in siege, and pacified Xiang.

sentences.zh: 還復領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He returned to his post as General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 侯景浮江西寇，軍次夏首。

translations.literal: Hou Jing floated west on the river to raid; his army halted at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sailed west on the river to raid; his army stopped at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 僧辯爲大都督，率巴州刺史淳于量、定州刺史杜龕、宜州刺史王琳、郴州刺史裴之橫等，俱赴西陽。

translations.literal: Sengbian as grand commander led the governor of Ba Chunyu Liang, the governor of Ding Du Kan, the governor of Yi Wang Lin, the governor of Chen Pei Zhihang, and others, all hurrying to Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian as grand commander led Ba's Chunyu Liang, Ding's Du Kan, Yi's Wang Lin, Chen's Pei Zhihang, and others to Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 軍次巴陵，聞郢州已沒，僧辯因據巴陵城。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baling; hearing that Yingzhou had fallen, Sengbian thereupon held Baling city.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Baling; hearing Yingzhou had fallen, Sengbian held Baling.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃命羅州刺史徐嗣徽、武州刺史杜崱並會僧辯于巴陵。

translations.literal: The Heir ordered the governor of Luo Xu Siwei and the governor of Wu Du Kan both to join Sengbian at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir ordered Luo's Xu Siwei and Wu's Du Kan to join Sengbian at Baling.

sentences.zh: 景旣陷郢城，兵衆益廣，徒黨甚銳，將進寇荊州。

translations.literal: Jing had already taken Ying city; his troops grew ever broader, his followers very sharp, and he was about to press the invasion of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had taken Ying; his troops swelled, his followers were keen, and he was about to invade Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃使偽儀同丁和統兵五千守江夏，大將宋子仙前驅一萬造巴陵，景悉凶徒水步繼進。

translations.literal: He sent the false Commissioner of Ceremonials Ding He with five thousand men to hold Jiangxia, the great general Song Zixian with ten thousand as vanguard to build Baling, and Jing himself followed with all his fierce followers by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: He sent false Commissioner Ding He with five thousand to hold Jiangxia, great general Song Zixian with ten thousand as vanguard against Baling, and Jing followed with all his fierce men by water and land.

sentences.zh: 於是緣江戍邏，望風請服，賊拓邏至于隱磯。

translations.literal: Thereupon the river garrisons along the route submitted at the wind's breath; the bandits extended their net to Yinji.
translations.idiomatic: River garrisons along the route submitted at a glance; the rebels spread their net to Yinji.

sentences.zh: 僧辯悉上江渚米糧，並沉公私船於水。

translations.literal: Sengbian sent all grain on the upper river sandbars upriver and sank public and private boats in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian sent all grain from the river islets upriver and sank public and private boats.

sentences.zh: 及賊前鋒次江口，僧辯乃分命衆軍，乘城固守，偃旗臥鼓，安若無人。

translations.literal: When the bandit vanguard reached the river mouth, Sengbian divided orders among the armies to man the walls and hold firm, lower banners and silence drums, calm as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel vanguard reached the river mouth, Sengbian ordered the armies to hold the walls, lower banners and silence drums, calm as if empty.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊衆濟江，輕騎至城下，問：「城內是誰？

translations.literal: The next day the bandit host crossed the river; light cavalry came below the wall and asked: "Who is in the city?
translations.idiomatic: Next day the rebels crossed the river; light horse came below the wall and asked, "Who holds the city?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「是王領軍。

translations.literal: " The answer came: "It is the Wang, General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: " The answer came, "General of the Guards Wang.

sentences.zh: 」賊曰：「語王領軍，事勢如此，何不早降？

translations.literal: " The bandits said: "Tell General Wang—the situation is thus; why not surrender early?
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels said, "Tell General Wang—the situation is what it is; why not surrender soon?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯使人答曰：「大軍但向荊州，此城自當非礙。

translations.literal: " Sengbian sent a man to answer: "The great army need only go to Jingzhou; this city will not be in the way.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian sent word, "The great army need only go to Jingzhou; this city will not hinder you.

sentences.zh: 僧辯百口在人掌握，豈得便降。

translations.literal: Sengbian's hundred mouths are in others' hands—how could he surrender at once?
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian's whole household is in your hands—how could he surrender at once?

sentences.zh: 」賊騎旣去，俄爾又來，曰：「我王已至，王領軍何爲不出與王相見邪？

translations.literal: " The bandit horsemen had barely left when before long they came again, saying: "Our king has arrived—General Wang, why do you not come out to meet our king?
translations.idiomatic: " The horsemen had barely left when they returned, saying, "Our king has come—General Wang, why not come out and meet him?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯不答。

translations.literal: " Sengbian did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian did not answer.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又執王珣等至於城下，珣爲書誘說城內。

translations.literal: Before long they brought Wang Xun and others below the wall; Xun wrote letters to entice those within.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they brought Wang Xun and others below the wall; Xun wrote to entice the garrison.

sentences.zh: 景帥船艦並集北寺，又分入港中，登岸治道，廣設氈屋，耀軍城東隴上，芟除草芿，開八道向城，遣五千兔頭肉薄苦攻。

translations.literal: Jing massed warships at North Temple and also sent detachments into the harbor mouths, came ashore to build roads, set out many felt tents, and displayed his army on the eastern ridge above the city; they mowed grass and opened eight roads toward the wall, sending five thousand rabbit-head assault troops in bitter close attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jing massed ships at North Temple, sent men into the harbors, came ashore to build roads and felt tents, displayed his host on the eastern ridge, mowed grass and opened eight approaches, and sent five thousand rabbit-head storm troops in bitter assault.

sentences.zh: 城內同時鼓噪，矢石雨下，殺賊旣多，賊乃引退。

translations.literal: Within the city they drummed and shouted at once; arrows and stones fell like rain and killed many bandits, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city they drummed and shouted; arrows and stones fell like rain, killed many rebels, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世祖又命平北將軍胡僧祐率兵下援僧辯。

translations.literal: The Heir again ordered the General Who Pacifies the North Hu Sengyou to lead troops down to reinforce Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir again ordered General Who Pacifies the North Hu Sengyou down with troops to reinforce Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊復攻巴陵，水步十處，鳴鼓吹脣，肉薄斫上。

translations.literal: That day the bandits again attacked Baling at ten points by water and land, beating drums and whistling, pressing close and hacking upward.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rebels again attacked Baling at ten points by water and land, drums and whistles, pressing close and hacking upward.

sentences.zh: 城上放木擲火爨昚石，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: From the wall they dropped timbers, cast fire, and hurled stones; casualties were very many.
translations.idiomatic: From the wall they dropped timbers, fire, and stones; casualties were very heavy.

sentences.zh: 午後賊退，乃更起長柵繞城，大列舸艦，以樓船攻水城西南角；

translations.literal: In the afternoon the bandits withdrew, then raised long palisades around the city and arrayed many warships, attacking the water gate at the southwest corner with tower ships;
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon the rebels withdrew, then raised long palisades and many warships, attacking the southwest water gate with tower ships;

sentences.zh: 又遣人渡洲岸，引䍧柯推蝦蟆車填壍，引障車臨城，二日方止。

translations.literal: they also sent men across the sandbar, drawing rakes and pushing tortoise rams to fill the moat, drawing screen wagons up to the wall—two days before they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: they also sent men across the sandbar with rakes and tortoise rams to fill the moat and screen wagons against the wall—two days before they stopped.

sentences.zh: 賊又於艦上豎木桔禋，聚茅置火，以燒水柵，風勢不利，自焚而退。

translations.literal: The bandits again set wooden siege towers on the ships, heaped straw and set fire to burn the water palisade; the wind was unfavorable and they burned themselves and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again raised wooden towers on the ships, heaped straw to burn the water palisade; wind turned against them and they burned themselves off.

sentences.zh: 旣頻戰挫衂，賊帥任約又爲陸法和所擒，景乃燒營夜遁，旋軍夏首。

translations.literal: Having suffered repeated defeats in battle, the bandit commander Ren Yue was also captured by Lu Fahe; Jing then burned his camp and fled by night, wheeling his army back to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats, rebel commander Ren Yue was captured by Lu Fahe; Jing burned camp and fled by night, wheeling back to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 世祖策勳行賞，以僧辯爲征東將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史，封長寧縣公。

translations.literal: The Heir assessed merit and gave rewards; Sengbian was made General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and governor of Jiangzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir assessed merit; Sengbian was made General Who Conquers the East, Commissioner with Golden Seal, governor of Jiangzhou, and Duke of Changning.

sentences.zh: 於是世祖命僧辯卽率巴陵諸軍，沿流討景。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Heir ordered Sengbian at once to lead the Baling armies downstream to pursue Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir ordered Sengbian at once to lead the Baling armies downstream against Jing.

sentences.zh: 師次郢城，步攻魯山。

translations.literal: The army halted at Ying city and attacked Lushan on foot.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Ying and attacked Lushan on foot.

sentences.zh: 魯山城主支化仁，景之騎將也，率其黨力戰，衆軍大破之，化仁乃降。

translations.literal: The Lushan garrison commander Zhi Huaren, a mounted general of Jing's, led his party in fierce fighting; the armies were greatly broken and Huaren then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's Zhi Huaren, Jing's cavalry general, fought fiercely; the armies broke him greatly and Huaren surrendered.

sentences.zh: 僧辯仍督諸軍渡江攻郢，卽入羅城。

translations.literal: Sengbian still supervised the armies in crossing the river to attack Ying and entered the outer city at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian still supervised the armies across the river against Ying and entered the outer city at once.

sentences.zh: 宋子仙蟻聚金城拒守，攻之未剋。

translations.literal: Song Zixian clustered like ants in the Golden City and held out; the attack did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian clustered in Golden City and held; the attack did not take it.

sentences.zh: 子仙使其黨時靈護率衆三千，開門出戰，僧辯又大破之，生擒靈護，斬首千級。

translations.literal: Zixian sent his follower Shi Linghu with three thousand men to open the gate and fight out; Sengbian again broke them greatly, captured Linghu alive, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian sent Shi Linghu with three thousand out the gate; Sengbian broke them again, captured Linghu alive, and beheaded over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 子仙衆退據倉門，帶江阻險，衆軍攻之，頻戰不剋。

translations.literal: Zixian's host withdrew to hold the granary gate, barred by the river's peril; the armies attacked but could not take it despite repeated battles.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian's men withdrew to the granary gate, river-barred and perilous; repeated attacks could not take it.

sentences.zh: 景旣聞魯山已沒，郢鎮復失羅城，乃率餘衆倍道歸建業。

translations.literal: Jing, hearing Lushan had fallen and Ying had lost the outer city, then led his remaining troops by double stages back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, hearing Lushan had fallen and Ying lost the outer city, raced the remnant back to Jiankang by double stages.

sentences.zh: 子仙等困蹙，計無所之，乞輸郢城，身還就景。

translations.literal: Zixian and the others were hard pressed with nowhere to go; they begged to hand over Ying city and return in person to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian and the others were trapped with nowhere to go; they begged to yield Ying and return to Jing in person.

sentences.zh: 僧辯偽許之，命給船百艘，以老其意。

translations.literal: Sengbian falsely agreed and ordered a hundred ships given them to dull their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian feigned agreement and ordered a hundred ships given to dull their intent.

sentences.zh: 子仙謂爲信然，浮舟將發，僧辯命杜龕率精勇千人，攀堞而上，同時鼓噪，掩至倉門。

translations.literal: Zixian thought it true; as the boats were about to set out, Sengbian ordered Du Kan to lead a thousand elite men up the battlements, and at once drums and shouts sounded as they burst upon the granary gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian believed it; as boats were about to sail, Sengbian ordered Du Kan with a thousand elites up the wall; drums and shouts burst on the granary gate.

sentences.zh: 水軍主宋遙率樓船，暗江四面雲合；

translations.literal: The river commander Song Yao led tower ships; on the hidden river the four quarters closed like clouds;
translations.idiomatic: River commander Song Yao led tower ships; on the hidden river four quarters closed like clouds;

sentences.zh: 子仙行戰行走，至于白楊浦，乃大破之，生擒子仙送江陵。

translations.literal: Zixian fought walking and fighting until he reached Baiyang Ford; there he was greatly broken, captured alive, and sent to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian fought on land and water until Baiyang Ford; there he was broken, captured alive, and sent to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 卽率諸軍進師九水。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the armies in advance to Jiushui.
translations.idiomatic: He then led the armies forward to Jiushui.

sentences.zh: 賊偽儀同范希榮、盧暉略尚據湓城，及僧辯軍至，希榮等因挾江州刺史臨城公棄城奔走。

translations.literal: The bandit false Commissioner Fan Xirong and Lu Huilue still held Tuncheng; when Sengbian's army arrived, Xirong and the others took the Prince of Lincheng, governor of Jiangzhou, and abandoned the city in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xirong and Lu Huilue still held Tuncheng; when Sengbian came, they seized the Prince of Lincheng, Jiangzhou governor, and fled the city.

sentences.zh: 世祖加僧辯侍中、尚書令、征東大將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: The Heir added Sengbian as palace attendant, Minister President, and General Who Conquers the East, granting one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir added palace attendant, Minister President, and General Who Conquers the East, with one set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 仍令僧辯且頓江州，須衆軍齊集，得時更進。

translations.literal: He still ordered Sengbian to halt at Jiangzhou until the armies gathered, then advance when the time came.
translations.idiomatic: He still ordered Sengbian to halt at Jiangzhou until the armies gathered, then advance in season.

sentences.zh: 頃之，世祖命江州衆軍悉同大舉，僧辯乃表皇帝凶問，告于江陵。

translations.literal: Before long the Heir ordered all Jiangzhou troops to join the great advance together; Sengbian then memorialized the emperor's grievous news and announced it at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Heir ordered all Jiangzhou troops on the great advance; Sengbian memorialized the emperor's death and announced it at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 仍率大將百餘人，連名勸世祖卽位；

translations.literal: He still led more than a hundred great generals in joint memorial urging the Heir to take the throne;
translations.idiomatic: He led more than a hundred great generals in joint memorial urging the Heir to the throne;

sentences.zh: 將欲進軍，又重奉表。

translations.literal: when he was about to march he again presented a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: when he was about to march he again memorialized.

sentences.zh: 雖未見從，並蒙優答。

translations.literal: Though he was not followed, all received gracious replies.
translations.idiomatic: Though not followed, all received gracious replies.

sentences.zh: 事見本紀。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the Basic Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is in the Basic Annals.

sentences.zh: 僧辯於是發自江州，直指建業，乃先命南兗州刺史侯瑱率銳卒輕舸，襲南陵、鵲頭等戍，至卽剋之。

translations.literal: Sengbian then set out from Jiangzhou straight for Jiankang; he first ordered the governor of South Yangzhou Hou Tian to lead crack troops in light boats to strike the garrisons at Nanling, Quetou, and others—they were taken as soon as he arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian set out from Jiangzhou straight for Jiankang; he first ordered South Yangzhou's Hou Tian with crack troops in light boats to strike Nanling, Quetou, and other garrisons—they fell at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳霸先率衆五萬，出自南江，前軍五千，行至湓口。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen Baxian had led fifty thousand men out from the southern river; the vanguard five thousand reached Tunkou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Baxian had led fifty thousand from the southern river; five thousand vanguard reached Tunkou.

sentences.zh: 霸先倜儻多謀策，名蓋僧辯，僧辯畏之。

translations.literal: Baxian was bold and full of stratagems; his fame overshadowed Sengbian, and Sengbian feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian was bold and full of stratagems; his fame overshadowed Sengbian, who feared him.

sentences.zh: 旣至湓口，與僧辯會于白茅洲，登壇盟誓。

translations.literal: When he reached Tunkou he met Sengbian at White Reed Ford; they ascended the altar and swore alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At Tunkou he met Sengbian at White Reed Ford; they ascended the altar and swore alliance.

sentences.zh: 霸先爲其文曰：「賊臣侯景，凶羯小胡，逆天無狀，構造姦惡；

translations.literal: Baxian drafted the text, saying: "The traitor minister Hou Jing, a vicious Di and petty barbarian, rebels against Heaven without measure and contrives wickedness and evil;
translations.idiomatic: Baxian drafted the text: "The traitor Hou Jing, a vicious Di and petty barbarian, rebels against Heaven without measure and contrives wickedness;

sentences.zh: 違背我恩義，破掠我國家，毒害我生民，移毀我社廟。

translations.literal: he has betrayed our grace and righteousness, plundered our state, poisoned our living people, and overturned and ruined our altars.
translations.idiomatic: he betrayed our grace, plundered our state, poisoned our people, and overturned our altars.

sentences.zh: 我高祖武皇帝靈聖聰明，光宅天下，劬勞兆庶，亭育萬民，如我考妣，五十所載。

translations.literal: Our High Ancestor the Martial Emperor was numinous and wise, his light dwelling over all under Heaven; he toiled for the myriad peoples and nurtured the ten thousand folk like father and mother—for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Our High Ancestor the Martial Emperor was numinous and wise, his light over all Heaven; he toiled for the myriad peoples and nurtured the ten thousand like father and mother—for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 哀景以窮見歸，全景將戮之首，置景要害之地，崇景非次之榮。

translations.literal: Pitying Jing who came in extremity he received him back; fully sparing Jing from the head that would be struck, he placed Jing in a vital position and heaped on him glory beyond his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying Jing in extremity he took him in; fully sparing him from execution, he placed Jing in a vital post and heaped unmerited glory on him.

sentences.zh: 我高祖於景何薄？

translations.literal: How were our High Ancestor and Jing ever shallow toward each other?
translations.idiomatic: What did our High Ancestor ever owe Jing?

sentences.zh: 我百姓於景何怨？

translations.literal: What grievance had our common people against Jing?
translations.idiomatic: What grievance had our people against Jing?

sentences.zh: 而景長戟強弩，陵蹙朝廷，鋸牙郊甸，殘食含靈。

translations.literal: Yet Jing with long halberd and strong crossbow pressed and crushed the court, sawed at the suburbs, and devoured those who bore spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jing with long halberd and strong crossbow pressed the court, sawed at the suburbs, and devoured the living.

sentences.zh: 刳肝斫趾，不曈其快；

translations.literal: He flayed livers and chopped toes and did not think it enough pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: He flayed livers and chopped toes and did not call it pleasure enough;

sentences.zh: 曝骨焚尸，不謂爲酷。

translations.literal: he exposed bones and burned corpses and did not call it cruel enough.
translations.idiomatic: he exposed bones and burned corpses and did not call it cruel enough.

sentences.zh: 高祖菲食卑宮，春秋九十，屈志凝威，憤終賊手。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor ate sparingly and dwelt in a low palace; in his ninetieth spring he bent his will and gathered wrath—yet died at the traitor's hand.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor ate sparingly and dwelt humbly; in his ninetieth spring he bent his will and gathered wrath—yet died at the traitor's hand.

sentences.zh: 大行皇帝溫嚴恭默，丕守鴻名，於景何有，復加忍毒。

translations.literal: The late emperor was warm, stern, reverent, and silent, greatly keeping the great name—what did he ever owe Jing, that Jing should add further poisonous cruelty?
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was warm, stern, reverent, and silent, keeping the great name—what did he owe Jing, that Jing should add further poison?

sentences.zh: 皇枝繦抱已上，緦功以還，窮刀極俎，旣屠且鱠。

translations.literal: Imperial branches in swaddling clothes and above, kin in hemp mourning and beyond—all met the extreme knife and chopping block, slaughtered and minced.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial branches in swaddling and above, kin in hemp mourning and beyond—all met the extreme knife and block, slaughtered and minced.

sentences.zh: 豈有率土之濱，謂爲王臣，食人之禾，飲人之水，忍聞此痛，而不悼心？

translations.literal: How can there be one who on the banks of all within the seas is called a king's minister, eats the people's grain, drinks the people's water, yet bears to hear this pain and not grieve in heart?
translations.idiomatic: How can one on all the banks within the seas be called the king's minister, eat the people's grain, drink the people's water, yet hear this pain and not grieve?

sentences.zh: 況臣僧辯、臣霸先等，荷稱國籓湘東王臣繹泣血銜哀之寄，摩頂至足之恩，世受先朝之德，身當將帥之任；

translations.literal: Moreover your subjects Sengbian and Baxian and others bear the Prince of Xiangdong's charge of weeping blood and holding grief in the mouth, the grace of rubbing crown to sole; generation after generation we have received the former court's virtue and personally bear the generals' charge—
translations.idiomatic: Moreover we subjects Sengbian and Baxian bear Prince of Xiangdong's charge of weeping blood and grief in the mouth, grace to crown and sole; generation after generation we received the former court's virtue and bear the generals' charge—

sentences.zh: 而不能瀝膽抽腸，共誅姦逆，雪天地之痛，報君父之仇，則不可以稟靈含識，戴天履地！

translations.literal: yet if we cannot pour out our gall and draw out our entrails to jointly execute the traitor, to wash away Heaven and Earth's pain and repay lord and father's enmity, then we cannot report to spirits who bear consciousness, nor bear Heaven above and tread Earth below!
translations.idiomatic: yet if we cannot pour gall and draw entrails to execute the traitor together, wash Heaven and Earth's pain and repay lord and father's enmity, we cannot face spirits with consciousness, nor bear Heaven and tread Earth!

sentences.zh: 今日相國至孝玄感，靈武斯發，已破賊徒，獲其元帥，止餘景身，尚在京邑。

translations.literal: Today the Prince, supremely filial and mysteriously moved, his numinous martial thus roused, has already broken the bandit host and captured their commander; only Jing's person remains, still in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Prince, supremely filial and mysteriously moved, his martial spirit roused, has broken the bandits and taken their commander; only Jing remains in the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣僧辯與臣霸先協和將帥，同心共契，必誅凶豎，尊奉相國，嗣膺鴻業，以主郊祭。

translations.literal: Your subjects Sengbian and Baxian harmonize the generals and join hearts in covenant; we must execute the vicious and honor the Prince, succeeding to the great enterprise and presiding over suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: We subjects Sengbian and Baxian harmonize the generals and join in covenant; we must kill the vicious, honor the Prince, succeed to the great enterprise, and preside at suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 前途若有一功，獲一賞，臣僧辯等不推己讓物，先身帥衆，則天地宗廟百神之靈，共誅共責。

translations.literal: If on the road ahead there is one merit or one reward, your subjects Sengbian and others will not push ourselves aside or yield the thing—we will lead the host in person—then the spirits of Heaven and Earth, the altars, and the hundred gods will jointly punish and jointly blame.
translations.idiomatic: If on the road there is one merit or one reward, we will not push aside or yield—we will lead the host in person—then Heaven and Earth, altars, and the hundred gods will jointly punish and blame.

sentences.zh: 臣僧辯、臣霸先同心共事，不相欺負，若有違戾，明神殛之。

translations.literal: Your subjects Sengbian and Baxian join hearts in the affair and will not deceive or fail each other; if there is violation, the bright spirits will strike us dead.
translations.idiomatic: We subjects Sengbian and Baxian join hearts and will not deceive each other; if we violate this, the bright spirits will strike us dead.

sentences.zh: 」於是升壇歃血，共讀盟文，皆淚下沾襟，辭色慷慨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they ascended the altar, drank blood, and together read the alliance text; all wept until their collars were wet, their words and bearing impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they ascended the altar, drank blood, and read the alliance together; all wept to wet their collars, impassioned in word and bearing.

sentences.zh: 及王師次於南洲，賊帥侯子鑒等率步騎萬餘人於岸挑戰，又以鵃䑠千艘並載士，兩邊悉八十棹，棹手皆越人，去來趣襲，捷過風電。

translations.literal: When the royal army halted at South Isle, the bandit commander Hou Zijian and others led more than ten thousand foot and horse to challenge battle on the bank; they also had more than a thousand war-boats each loaded with troops, both sides with eighty oars apiece, the oarsmen all Yue men—coming and going in swift raid, faster than wind and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: When the royal army halted at South Isle, rebel commander Hou Zijian and others led over ten thousand foot and horse to challenge on the bank; more than a thousand war-boats each loaded troops, both sides eighty oars, oarsmen all Yue men—raiding faster than wind and lightning.

sentences.zh: 僧辯乃麾細船，皆令退縮，悉使大艦夾泊兩岸。

translations.literal: Sengbian waved the light boats all to draw back and made the great ships moor close along both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian waved the light boats back and moored great ships along both banks.

sentences.zh: 賊謂水軍欲退，爭出趨之，衆軍乃棹大艦，截其歸路，鼓噪大呼，合戰中江，賊悉赴水。

translations.literal: The bandits thought the river army meant to retreat and all rushed out to pursue; the armies then rowed the great ships to cut their return, drums and shouts roaring, joining battle mid-river—the bandits all threw themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels thought the fleet was retreating and rushed out; the armies rowed great ships to cut their return, drums and shouts mid-river—the rebels all threw themselves into the water.

sentences.zh: 僧辯卽督諸軍沿流而下，進軍于石頭之斗城，作連營以逼賊。

translations.literal: Sengbian at once supervised the armies downstream, advancing to Dou City at Stone Hill, building linked camps to press the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian at once led the armies downstream to Dou City at Stone Hill and built linked camps to press the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊乃橫嶺上築五城拒守，侯景自出，與王師大戰於石頭城北。

translations.literal: The bandits then built five cities across the ridge to hold out; Hou Jing came out himself and fought the royal army greatly north of Stone Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built five cities across the ridge; Hou Jing came out himself and fought the royal army greatly north of Stone Hill.

sentences.zh: 霸先謂僧辯曰：「醜虜遊魂，貫盈已稔，逋誅送死，欲爲一決。

translations.literal: Baxian said to Sengbian: "The ugly bandit is a wandering soul; his guilt is full and ripe—fleeing execution he comes to die, wishing for one decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian told Sengbian, "The ugly bandit is a wandering soul; his guilt is full—fleeing the executioner he comes to die and wants one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 我衆賊寡，且分其勢。

translations.literal: Our host is many and the bandit few—let us divide their force.
translations.idiomatic: We are many and they few—divide their force.

sentences.zh: 」卽遣強弩二千張，攻賊西面兩城，仍使結陣以當賊。

translations.literal: " He at once sent two thousand strong crossbows to attack the bandits' two western cities and still arrayed ranks to meet the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent two thousand strong crossbows against the rebels' two western cities and still arrayed ranks to meet them.

sentences.zh: 僧辯在後麾軍而進，復大破之。

translations.literal: Sengbian in the rear waved the army forward and again broke them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian in the rear waved the army on and broke them again.

sentences.zh: 盧暉略聞景戰敗，以石頭城降，僧辯引軍入據之。

translations.literal: Lu Huilue, hearing Jing was defeated in battle, surrendered Stone City; Sengbian led the army in to occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huilue, hearing Jing was beaten, surrendered Stone City; Sengbian entered and held it.

sentences.zh: 景之退也，北走朱方，於是景散兵走告僧辯，僧辯令衆將入據臺城。

translations.literal: When Jing retreated he fled north to Zhufang; then Jing's scattered soldiers came reporting to Sengbian, and Sengbian ordered the generals to enter and hold Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing retreated north to Zhufang, scattered soldiers reported to Sengbian, and he ordered the generals into Terrace City.

sentences.zh: 其夜，軍人采梠失火，燒太極殿及東西堂等。

translations.literal: That night soldiers gathering firewood started a fire that burned the Hall of Supreme Pole and the eastern and western halls.
translations.idiomatic: That night soldiers gathering firewood set a fire that burned the Hall of Supreme Pole and the eastern and western halls.

sentences.zh: 時軍人鹵掠京邑，剝剔士庶，民爲其執縛者，衵衣不免。

translations.literal: At the time soldiers plundered the capital, stripping gentry and commoners; those seized by them could not keep even a single garment.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers plundered the capital, stripping gentry and commoners; those seized could not keep a single garment.

sentences.zh: 盡驅逼居民以求購贖，自石頭至于東城，緣淮號叫之聲，震響京邑，於是百姓失望。

translations.literal: They drove and pressed the residents to ransom themselves; from Stone Hill to the eastern city, along the Huai the cries of appeal shook the capital—thereupon the people lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: They drove residents for ransom; from Stone Hill to the eastern city cries along the Huai shook the capital—the people lost hope.

sentences.zh: 僧辯命侯瑱、裴之橫率精甲五千，東入討景。

translations.literal: Sengbian ordered Hou Tian and Pei Zhihheng to lead five thousand elite armored troops east to pursue Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian ordered Hou Tian and Pei Zhihheng with five thousand elites east to pursue Jing.

sentences.zh: 僧辯收賊黨王偉等二十餘人，送于江陵。

translations.literal: Sengbian seized more than twenty of Jing's party including Wang Wei and sent them to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian seized more than twenty of Jing's party including Wang Wei and sent them to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 偽行臺趙伯超自吳松江降於侯瑱，瑱時送至僧辯。

translations.literal: The false Mobile Headquarters Zhao Bochao surrendered from the Wu Song River to Hou Tian; Tian at the time delivered him to Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: False Mobile Headquarters Zhao Bochao surrendered from Wu Song River to Hou Tian, who delivered him to Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 僧辯謂伯超曰：「趙公，卿荷國重恩，遂復同逆。

translations.literal: Sengbian said to Bochao: "Master Zhao, you bore the state's heavy grace yet again joined the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian told Bochao, "Master Zhao, you bore the state's heavy grace yet joined the rebellion again.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，將欲何如？

translations.literal: Today's affair—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair—what will you do?

sentences.zh: 」因命送江陵。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered him sent to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him sent to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 伯超旣出，僧辯顧坐客曰：「朝廷昔唯知有趙伯超耳，豈識王僧辯？

translations.literal: After Bochao went out Sengbian looked at the seated guests and said: "The court in former days knew only Zhao Bochao—who knew Wang Sengbian?
translations.idiomatic: After Bochao left Sengbian looked at the guests and said, "The court once knew only Zhao Bochao—who knew Wang Sengbian?

sentences.zh: 社稷旣傾，爲我所復；

translations.literal: The altars had already toppled and were restored by me;
translations.idiomatic: The altars had toppled and I restored them;

sentences.zh: 人之興廢，亦復何常。

translations.literal: the rise and fall of men—how can it be constant?
translations.idiomatic: the rise and fall of men—how can it stay constant?

sentences.zh: 」賓客皆前稱歎功德。

translations.literal: " The guests all came forward praising his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " The guests all came forward praising his merit.

sentences.zh: 僧辯瞿然，乃謬答曰：「此乃聖上之威德，羣帥之用命。

translations.literal: Sengbian started in alarm and falsely answered: "This is the sage sovereign's majestic virtue and the host of generals' obedience to orders.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian started, then falsely answered, "This is the sage sovereign's majesty and the generals' obedience.

sentences.zh: 老夫雖濫居戎首，何力之有焉？

translations.literal: This old man may occupy the army's head in name—what strength is there in me?
translations.idiomatic: This old man may sit at the army's head in name—what strength have I?

sentences.zh: 」於是逆寇悉平，京都剋定。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the rebellious bandits were all pacified and the capital was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the rebels were all pacified and the capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽帝位，以僧辯功，進授鎮衛將軍、司徒，加班劍二十人，改封永寧郡公，食邑五千戶，侍中、尚書令、鼓吹並如故。

translations.literal: The Heir took the imperial throne; for Sengbian's merit he was promoted to General Who Guards the Realm, Grand Minister, with twenty ceremonial swords added, enfeoffed Duke of Yongning commandery with a fief of five thousand households; palace attendant, Minister President, and martial music all as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir took the throne; for Sengbian's merit he was promoted General Who Guards the Realm and Grand Minister, twenty ceremonial swords, Duke of Yongning with five thousand households; palace attendant, Minister President, and martial music unchanged.

sentences.zh: 是後湘州賊陸納等攻破衡州刺史丁道貴於淥口，盡收其軍實；

translations.literal: Afterward the Xiang bandit Lu Na and others broke the governor of Heng Ding Daogui at Lukou and seized all his military stores;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Xiang bandit Lu Na and others broke Heng governor Ding Daogui at Lukou and seized all his stores;

sentences.zh: 李洪雅又自零陵率衆出空靈灘，稱助討納。

translations.literal: Li Hongya also led a host from Lingling out through Kongling Ford, claiming to aid the campaign against Na.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongya also led men from Lingling out Kongling Ford, claiming to aid the campaign against Na.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未達其心，深以爲慮，乃遣中書舍人羅重歡徵僧辯上就驃騎將軍宜豊侯循南征。

translations.literal: The court had not yet understood his heart and was deeply worried; it sent the palace gentleman Luo Chonghuan to summon Sengbian up to join the General of Swift Cavalry the Marquis of Yifeng Xun on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The court had not read his heart and was deeply worried; it sent palace gentleman Luo Chonghuan to summon Sengbian to join Swift Cavalry Marquis of Yifeng Xun south.

sentences.zh: 僧辯因督杜崱等衆軍，發於建業，師次巴陵。

translations.literal: Sengbian thereupon supervised Du Kan and the other armies, setting out from Jiankang; the army halted at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian supervised Du Kan and the other armies from Jiankang; the army halted at Baling.

sentences.zh: 詔僧辯爲都督東上諸軍事，霸先爲都督西上諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict made Sengbian commander of eastern-upper military affairs and Baxian commander of western-upper military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Sengbian commander of eastern-upper forces and Baxian commander of western-upper forces.

sentences.zh: 先時霸先讓都督于僧辯，僧辯不受，故世祖分爲東西都督，而俱南討焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Baxian had yielded the command to Sengbian, and Sengbian did not accept; therefore the Heir divided eastern and western commanders, and both marched south together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Baxian had yielded command to Sengbian, who refused; the Heir therefore split eastern and western command, and both marched south.

sentences.zh: 時納等下據車輪，夾岸爲城，前斷水勢，士卒驍猛，皆百戰之餘。

translations.literal: At the time Na and the others held downstream at Chelun, building cities on both banks, cutting the water's force; their soldiers were fierce and bold, all veterans of a hundred battles.
translations.idiomatic: Na held Chelun downstream, cities on both banks, cutting the water; his soldiers were fierce, all veterans of a hundred battles.

sentences.zh: 僧辯憚之，不與輕進，於是稍作連城以逼賊。

translations.literal: Sengbian feared them and did not advance lightly; he thereupon built linked walls bit by bit to press the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian feared them and would not advance lightly; he built linked walls bit by bit to press them.

sentences.zh: 賊見不敢交鋒，並懷懈怠。

translations.literal: The bandits saw they dared not cross blades and all grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw no crossing of blades and grew slack.

sentences.zh: 僧辯因其無備，命諸軍水步攻之，親執旗鼓，以誡進止。

translations.literal: Sengbian used their lack of preparation and ordered the armies to attack by water and land; he personally held drum and banner to warn advance and halt.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian used their unreadiness and ordered attack by water and land; he held drum and banner himself to command advance and halt.

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍競出，大戰於車輪，與驃騎循並力苦攻，陷其二城。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies all rushed out and fought a great battle at Chelun; with the Swift Cavalry Xun they joined in bitter attack and took two of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: The armies rushed out and fought greatly at Chelun; with Swift Cavalry Xun they joined in bitter attack and took two cities.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，步走歸保長沙，驅逼居民，入城拒守。

translations.literal: The bandits were greatly defeated and fled on foot back to hold Changsha, driving and pressing the residents to enter the city and hold out.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were greatly defeated and fled on foot to Changsha, driving residents into the city to hold.

sentences.zh: 僧辯追躡，乃命築壘圍之，悉令諸軍廣建圍柵，僧辯出坐壟上而自臨視。

translations.literal: Sengbian pursued; he ordered ramparts built to besiege them and ordered all armies to raise broad siege palisades; Sengbian sat on the mound and personally oversaw.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian pursued, ordered ramparts and broad siege palisades, and sat on the mound overseeing himself.

sentences.zh: 賊望，識僧辯，知不設備，賊黨吳藏、李賢明等乃率銳卒千人，開門掩出，蒙楯直進，徑趨僧辯。

translations.literal: The bandits looked out, recognized Sengbian, and knew he was unprepared; the bandit party Wu Zang, Li Xianming, and others then led a thousand crack troops to burst out the gate with shields, charging straight at Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels looked out, recognized Sengbian, knew he was unprepared; Wu Zang, Li Xianming, and others led a thousand crack troops out the gate with shields straight at Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 時杜崱、杜龕並侍左右，帶甲衛者止百餘人，因下遣人與賊交戰。

translations.literal: At the time Du Qi and Du Kan both attended at his side; armored guards numbered only a little more than a hundred; he sent men down to fight the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi and Du Kan attended at his side; armored guards were only a little over a hundred; he sent men down to fight.

sentences.zh: 李賢明乘鎧馬，從者十騎，大呼衝突，僧辯尚據胡床，不爲之動。

translations.literal: Li Xianming rode armored horse with ten followers following, shouting and charging; Sengbian still sat on his folding chair unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianming rode armored horse with ten followers, shouting and charging; Sengbian still sat on his folding chair unmoved.

sentences.zh: 於是指揮勇敢，遂獲賢明，因卽斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he directed the brave and captured Xianming, and at once beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the brave, captured Xianming, and beheaded him at once.

sentences.zh: 賊乃退歸城內。

translations.literal: The bandits then withdrew into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels withdrew into the city.

sentences.zh: 初，陸納阻兵內逆，以王琳爲辭，云「朝廷若放王琳，納等自當降伏」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lu Na obstructed the army in internal rebellion, he used Wang Lin as his plea, saying: "If the court releases Wang Lin, Na and the others will themselves surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lu Na obstructed the army in rebellion and used Wang Lin as plea, saying, "If the court releases Wang Lin, Na and the others will surrender.

sentences.zh: 于時衆軍並進，未之許也。

translations.literal: " At the time the armies were all advancing and it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The armies were all advancing and it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 而武陵王擁衆上流，內外駭懼，世祖乃遣琳和解之。

translations.literal: But the Prince of Wuling held a host on the upper stream; inside and outside were terrified; the Heir then sent Lin to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: But Prince of Wuling held a host upstream; inside and outside were terrified; the Heir sent Lin to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 至是，湘州平。

translations.literal: By then Xiangzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiangzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 僧辯旋于江陵，因被詔會衆軍西討，督舟師二萬，輿駕出天居寺餞行。

translations.literal: Sengbian returned to Jiangling and, by edict, gathered the armies for the western campaign, supervising twenty thousand river troops; the imperial carriage came out to Heavenly Dwelling Temple to see them off.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian returned to Jiangling and by edict gathered armies for the western campaign, supervising twenty thousand river troops; the carriage came to Heavenly Dwelling Temple to see them off.

sentences.zh: 俄而武陵敗績，僧辯自枝江班師于江陵，旋鎮建業。

translations.literal: Before long Wuling was defeated; Sengbian withdrew from Zhijiang to Jiangling and soon garrisoned Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wuling was defeated; Sengbian withdrew from Zhijiang to Jiangling and soon garrisoned Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 是月，居少時，復回江陵。

translations.literal: That month, after dwelling only a short time, he returned again to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: That month, after dwelling only briefly, he returned again to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 齊主高洋遣郭元建率衆二萬，大列舟艦於合肥，將謀襲建業，又遣其大將邢景遠、步六汗薩、東方老等率衆繼之。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler Gao Yang sent Guo Yuanjian with twenty thousand men, arraying many warships at Hefei, intending to raid Jiankang; he also sent his great generals Xing Jingyuan, Buluohan Sa, Dongfang Lao, and others with troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qi ruler Gao Yang sent Guo Yuanjian with twenty thousand, many warships at Hefei, intending to raid Jiankang; he also sent great generals Xing Jingyuan, Buluohan Sa, Dongfang Lao, and others to follow.

sentences.zh: 時陳霸先鎮建康，旣聞此事，馳報江陵。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Baxian garrisoned Jiankang; hearing this he raced word to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian garrisoned Jiankang; hearing this he raced word to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽詔僧辯次于姑孰，卽留鎮焉。

translations.literal: The Heir at once ordered Sengbian to halt at Gushu and remain to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir ordered Sengbian to halt at Gushu and garrison there.

sentences.zh: 先命豫州刺史侯瑱率精甲三千人築壘於東關，以拒北寇；

translations.literal: He first ordered the governor of Yu Hou Tian to lead three thousand elite armored men to build ramparts at East Pass to resist the northern invaders;
translations.idiomatic: He first ordered Yu governor Hou Tian with three thousand elites to build ramparts at East Pass against the northern invaders;

sentences.zh: 徵吳郡太守張彪、吳興太守裴之橫會瑱於關；

translations.literal: he summoned the governor of Wu Commandery Zhang Biao and the governor of Wuxing Pei Zhihheng to join Tian at the pass;
translations.idiomatic: he summoned Wu governor Zhang Biao and Wuxing governor Pei Zhihheng to join Tian at the pass;

sentences.zh: 因與北軍戰，大敗之，僧辯率衆軍振旅于建業。

translations.literal: they fought the northern army and broke it greatly; Sengbian led the mass of armies in triumphant return to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: they fought the northern army and broke it greatly; Sengbian led the armies in triumphant return to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年二月甲辰，詔曰：「贊俊遂賢，稱于秦典；

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Chengsheng, on the day jiachen, an edict said: "Promoting the worthy and advancing the able was praised in Qin's canons;
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year three, second month, day jiachen, an edict said, "Promoting the worthy and advancing the able was praised in Qin's canons;

sentences.zh: 自上安下，聞之漢制。

translations.literal: ordering from above and securing below was heard in Han's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: ordering from above and securing below was heard in Han's institutions.

sentences.zh: 所以仰協台曜，俯佐弘圖。

translations.literal: Therefore one looks up to harmonize the terrace stars and looks down to assist the great design.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one looks up to harmonize the terrace stars and looks down to assist the great design.

sentences.zh: 使持節、侍中、司徒、尚書令、都督揚、南徐、東揚三州諸軍事、鎮衛將軍、揚州刺史、永寧郡開國公僧辯，器宇凝深，風格詳遠，行爲士則，言表身文，學貫九流，武該七略。

translations.literal: Bearer of the staff, palace attendant, Grand Minister, Minister President, commander of military affairs in Yang, South Xu, and East Yang provinces, General Who Guards the Realm, governor of Yangzhou, Duke of Yongning commandery the Opening State Wang Sengbian—his vessel is deep and settled, his style detailed and far-reaching; in conduct he is the scholar's measure, in speech and appearance he bodies the literary; in learning he spans the nine streams, in martial affairs he covers the seven summaries.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the staff, palace attendant, Grand Minister, Minister President, commander in Yang, South Xu, and East Yang, General Who Guards the Realm, Yangzhou governor, Opening Duke of Yongning Wang Sengbian—vessel deep and settled, style detailed and far; conduct is the scholar's measure, speech and bearing body the literary; learning spans nine streams, martial covers seven summaries.

sentences.zh: 頃歲征討，自西徂東；

translations.literal: In recent years in campaigns from west to east—
translations.idiomatic: In recent campaigns from west to east—

sentences.zh: 師不疲勞，民無怨讟；

translations.literal: the armies were not weary, the people had no complaint;
translations.idiomatic: the armies were not weary, the people had no complaint;

sentences.zh: 王業艱難，實兼夷險。

translations.literal: the royal enterprise was arduous, truly mixing barbarian peril.
translations.idiomatic: the royal enterprise was arduous, truly mixing barbarian peril.

sentences.zh: 宜其燮此中台，膺茲上將；

translations.literal: He should harmonize this central terrace and bear this upper generalship;
translations.idiomatic: He should harmonize this central terrace and bear this upper generalship;

sentences.zh: 寄之經野，匡我朝猷。

translations.literal: Entrust to the realm's governance and buttress our court's plans.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust him with rule across the realm and strengthen our court's design.

sentences.zh: 加太尉、車騎大將軍，餘悉如故。」

translations.literal: Promote him to Grand Commandant and General of Chariots and Cavalry; all else as before."
translations.idiomatic: Promote him to Grand Commandant and General of Chariots and Cavalry; all else unchanged."

sentences.zh: 頃之，丁母太夫人憂，世祖遣侍中謁者監護喪事，策諡曰貞敬太夫人。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he entered mourning for his mother, the Lady Grand Mistress; Emperor Yuan sent a palace attendant and imperial messenger to oversee the funeral rites and issued a posthumous title: the Upright and Reverent Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he mourned his mother, Lady Grand Mistress; Yuan sent an attendant and imperial messenger to supervise the funeral and posthumously titled her Upright and Reverent Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 夫人姓魏氏。

translations.literal: The lady's surname was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Her surname was Wei.

sentences.zh: 神念以天監初董率徒衆據東關，退保合肥漅湖西，因娶以爲室，生僧辯。

translations.literal: When Shennian in the early Heavenly Surveillance era led his followers to hold the eastern pass and then withdrew to guard west of Chaohu at Hefei, he took her in marriage; she bore Sengbian.
translations.idiomatic: When Shennian early in Heavenly Surveillance held the eastern pass and withdrew to Hefei west of Chaohu, he married her and she bore Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 性甚安和，善於綏接，家門內外，莫不懷之。

translations.literal: By nature she was very gentle and skilled at winning people over; within and without the household none did not cherish her.
translations.idiomatic: She was gentle by nature and won people over; everyone in the household cherished her.

sentences.zh: 初，僧辯下獄，夫人流淚徒行，將入謝罪，世祖不與相見。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sengbian was imprisoned, the lady went on foot in tears to enter the palace and beg forgiveness; Emperor Yuan would not receive her.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was imprisoned, she walked to court in tears to beg pardon; Yuan would not see her.

sentences.zh: 時貞惠世子有寵於世祖，軍國大事多關領焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Heir of Zhenhui was favored by Emperor Yuan, and most state and military affairs passed through his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir of Zhenhui was then in favor with Yuan, and most state and military affairs ran through him.

sentences.zh: 夫人詣閤，自陳無訓，涕泗嗚咽，衆並憐之。

translations.literal: The lady went to the gate lodge, declaring herself without proper teaching; weeping and sobbing, all pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: She came to the gate lodge, blamed herself for poor upbringing, and wept until all pitied her.

sentences.zh: 及僧辯免出，夫人深相責勵，辭色俱嚴，云：「人之事君，惟須忠烈，非但保祐當世，亦乃慶流子孫。

translations.literal: When Sengbian was released, the lady sternly reproved and exhorted him, her words and countenance both severe, saying: "In serving one's lord one must be loyal and fierce—not only to protect the age but also to extend blessing to one's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was freed, she rebuked him sternly: "Serving a lord demands loyalty and fierceness—not only to shield the age but to bless your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」及僧辯剋復舊京，功蓋天下，夫人恒自謙損，不以富貴驕物。

translations.literal: " When Sengbian recovered the old capital his merit covered the realm; the lady always restrained herself and did not flaunt wealth and rank before others.
translations.idiomatic: " After he recovered the old capital his merit covered the realm; she always held herself back and never flaunted rank.

sentences.zh: 朝野咸共稱之，謂爲明哲婦人也。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike praised her, calling her a wise and discerning woman.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside praised her as a wise woman.

sentences.zh: 及旣薨殞，甚見愍悼。

translations.literal: When she had died, she was deeply mourned.
translations.idiomatic: At her death she was deeply mourned.

sentences.zh: 且以僧辯勳業隆重，故喪禮加焉。

translations.literal: Because Sengbian's achievements were weighty, the funeral rites were augmented.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sengbian's service was great, her funeral rites were augmented.

sentences.zh: 靈柩將歸建康，又遣謁者至舟渚弔祭。

translations.literal: As the coffin was to return to Jiankang, the emperor again sent an imperial messenger to the river landing to offer libation.
translations.idiomatic: As the coffin was to return to Jiankang, he again sent a messenger to libate at the river landing.

sentences.zh: 命尚書左僕射王裒爲其文曰：「維爾世基武子，族懋陽元，金相比映，玉德齊溫。

translations.literal: He ordered the Minister of the Left, Wang Pou, to compose her text, which read: "Alas for you, foundation of the age, scion of martial lineage, clan glorious in Yangyuan, gold and jade reflecting one another, jade virtue matching warmth.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Minister of the Left Wang Pou to compose her text: "Alas for you, foundation of the age, scion of martial lineage, clan glorious in Yangyuan, gold and jade reflecting one another, jade virtue matching warmth.

sentences.zh: 旣稱女則，兼循婦言。

translations.idiomatic: Turning south, indignant sighs fill my breast.

translations.idiomatic: I take all under Heaven as my house and the Great Way as what aids all things.
