sentences.zh: 齊朝大德，信感神民。

translations.literal: Great Qi's vast virtue—faith moving gods and people.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi's vast virtue moved gods and people.

sentences.zh: 方仰藉皇威，敬憑元宰，討逆賊於咸陽，誅叛子於雲夢，同心協力，克定邦家。

translations.literal: Now we look up to rely on imperial might and respectfully lean on the chief minister to punish rebels at Xianyang and execute traitors at Yunmeng—with one heart and united strength to settle the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now we rely on imperial might and lean on the chief minister to punish rebels at Xianyang and traitors at Yunmeng—with one heart to settle the state.

sentences.zh: 覽所示權景宣書，上流諸將，本有忠略，棄親向讎，庶當不爾，防奸定亂，終在於公。

translations.literal: Reading the Quan Jingxuan letter you showed, the upriver generals originally had loyal designs; to abandon kin and turn to the foe—they surely would not; preventing treachery and settling chaos ultimately rests with you.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Quan Jingxuan's letter you showed, upriver generals had loyal designs; to abandon kin for the foe they surely would not—preventing treachery rests with you.

sentences.zh: 今且頓東關，更待來信，未知水陸何處見迎。

translations.literal: For now we halt at the eastern pass and await further word—do not know where on water or land you will welcome us.
translations.idiomatic: For now we halt at the eastern pass and await word—where on water or land will you welcome us?

sentences.zh: 夫建國立君，布在方策，入盟出質，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Founding a state and setting up a ruler are set down in the records; entering alliance and sending hostages has its own long precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Founding a state and setting a ruler are in the records; alliance and hostages have long precedent.

sentences.zh: 若公之忠節，上感蒼旻；

translations.literal: If your loyal integrity moves the azure heavens;
translations.idiomatic: If your loyal integrity moves heaven;

sentences.zh: 羣帥同謀，必匪攜貳。

translations.literal: the commanders in common counsel surely are not of divided allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: the commanders in common counsel are surely not divided.

sentences.zh: 則齊師反斾，義不陵江，如致爽言，誓以無克。

translations.literal: Then Qi's army will turn its banners and by righteousness will not cross the Yangtze; if contrary words are sent, I vow we shall not conquer.
translations.idiomatic: Then Qi's army will turn its banners and by righteousness will not cross the Yangtze; if contrary words are sent, I vow we shall not conquer.

sentences.zh: 韜旗側席，遲復行人。

translations.literal: Lower the flags and sit sidewise—awaiting the envoy's return.
translations.idiomatic: Lower the flags and sit sidewise—awaiting the envoy's return.

sentences.zh: 曹沖奉表齊都，卽押送也。

translations.literal: Cao Chong presents a memorial to the Qi capital and is detained and sent at once.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Chong presents a memorial to Qi and is detained and sent at once.

sentences.zh: 渭橋之下，惟遲敘言；

translations.literal: Below Weiqiao I only await your words;
translations.idiomatic: Below Weiqiao I only await your words;

sentences.zh: 汜水之陽，預有號懼。

translations.literal: south of the Sishui I already have the cry of fear."
translations.idiomatic: south of the Sishui I already have the cry of fear."

sentences.zh: 」僧辯又重啟曰：「員外常侍姜暠還，奉敕伏具動止。

translations.literal: " Sengbian again memorialized: "Regular Attendant Jiang Gao has returned bearing your edict; bowing low I have received your movements.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian again memorialized, "Regular Attendant Jiang Gao has returned with your edict; bowing low I have your movements.

sentences.zh: 大齊仁義之風，曲被鄰國，卹災救難，申此大猷。

translations.literal: Great Qi's wind of benevolence and righteousness bends graciously on a neighboring state; pitying disaster and rescuing hardship—this great design is declared.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi's benevolence bends on a neighbor; pitying disaster and rescuing hardship declares this great design.

sentences.zh: 皇家枝戚，莫不榮荷；

translations.literal: The imperial clan's kin—none do not glory in the burden;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan—none do not glory in the burden;

sentences.zh: 江東冠冕，俱知憑賴。

translations.literal: the crowned heads east of the Yangtze all know whom to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: the crowned heads east of the Yangtze all know whom to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今歃不忘信，信實由衷，謹遣臣第七息顯，顯所生劉並弟子世珍，往彼充質；

translations.literal: Today the oath is not to forget faith—faith truly comes from the heart; I respectfully send my seventh son Xian, Xian's mother Liu, and my nephew Shizhen to go there as hostages;
translations.idiomatic: Today the oath does not forget faith—faith comes from the heart; I send my seventh son Xian, his mother Liu, and nephew Shizhen as hostages;

sentences.zh: 仍遣左民尚書周弘正至歷陽奉迎。

translations.literal: and I also send Minister of the Left Zhou Hongzheng to Liyang to welcome you.
translations.idiomatic: and send Minister of the Left Zhou Hongzheng to Liyang to welcome you.

sentences.zh: 艫舳浮江，俟一龍之渡；

translations.literal: Warships float on the river, awaiting the one dragon's crossing;
translations.idiomatic: Warships float on the river, awaiting the dragon's crossing;

sentences.zh: 清宮丹陛，候六傳之入。

translations.literal: the pure palace and cinnabar steps await the six relays' entry.
translations.idiomatic: the pure palace and cinnabar steps await the six relays' entry.

sentences.zh: 萬國傾心，同榮晉文之反；

translations.literal: The myriad states bend their hearts—together they glory in Duke Wen of Jin's return;
translations.idiomatic: The myriad states bend their hearts—together they glory in Duke Wen's return;

sentences.zh: 三善克宣，方流宋昌之議。

translations.literal: the three goods can be proclaimed—flowing in Song Chang's discourse.
translations.idiomatic: the three goods can be proclaimed—in Song Chang's discourse.

sentences.zh: 國祚旣隆，社稷有奉。

translations.literal: The dynastic fortune is already lofty; the altars have support.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic fortune is lofty; the altars have support.

sentences.zh: 則羣臣竭節，報厚施于大齊；

translations.literal: Then the ministers will exhaust their integrity, repaying Great Qi's thick favor;
translations.idiomatic: Then ministers will exhaust integrity, repaying Great Qi's favor;

sentences.zh: 戮力展愚，效忠誠於陛下。

translations.literal: they will deploy their utmost loyalty to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: they will show utmost loyalty to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今遣吏部尚書王通奉啓以聞。

translations.literal: Now I send Minister of Personnel Wang Tong to present this memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Now I send Minister of Personnel Wang Tong to present this memorial."

sentences.zh: 」僧辯因求以敬帝爲皇太子。

translations.literal: Sengbian thereupon asked that Emperor Jing be made heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian then asked that Emperor Jing be made heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 貞陽又答曰：「王尚書通至，復枉示，知欲遣賢弟世珍以表誠質，具悉憂國之懷。

translations.literal: Zhenyang again replied: "Wang Tong, Minister of Personnel, has arrived and again wrongly shows that you wish to send your worthy younger brother Shizhen to display sincerity—I fully know your heart anxious for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyang replied, "Minister Wang Tong has arrived and shows you wish to send your nephew Shizhen as pledge—I know your heart anxious for the state.

sentences.zh: 復以庭中玉樹，掌內明珠，無累胸懷，志在匡救，豈非劬勞我社稷，弘濟我邦家？

translations.literal: Again you offer the jade tree in the courtyard and the bright pearl in the palm—no burden on the breast, the will set on rescue—is this not toiling for our altars and grandly aiding our house?
translations.idiomatic: Again you offer the courtyard jade tree and palm bright pearl—no burden on the breast, the will on rescue—is this not toiling for our altars and aiding our house?

sentences.zh: 慚歎之懷，用忘興寢。

translations.literal: The feeling of shame and sighing makes one forget to rise or sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Shame and sighing make one forget to rise or sleep.

sentences.zh: 晉安王東京貽厥之重，西都繼體之賢，嗣守皇家，寧非民望。

translations.literal: Prince Jin'an's weight as heir in the eastern capital and the western capital's worth as successor in the line—to continue guarding the imperial house is surely the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin'an's weight in the eastern capital and the western capital heir's worth—to continue the house is the people's hope.

sentences.zh: 但世道喪亂，宜立長君，以其蒙孽，難可承業。

translations.literal: But the age is in chaos and ruin—a mature ruler should be set up; because he bears misfortune, it is hard to undertake the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: But the age is in chaos—a mature ruler should be set up; because he bears misfortune, he cannot undertake the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 成、昭之德，自古希儔；

translations.literal: The virtue of Cheng and Zhao is rare since antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of Cheng and Zhao is rare since antiquity;

sentences.zh: 沖、質之危，何代無此。

translations.literal: the peril of Chong and Zhi—which age has lacked it?
translations.idiomatic: the peril of Chong and Zhi—which age has lacked it?

sentences.zh: 孤身當否運，志不圖生。

translations.literal: Alone I meet an unkind age; my will is not to scheme for life.
translations.idiomatic: Alone I meet an unkind age; my will is not to live for myself.

sentences.zh: 忽荷不世之恩，仍致非常之舉。

translations.literal: Suddenly I bear an unworldly grace and again meet an extraordinary elevation.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly I bear unworldly grace and meet extraordinary elevation.

sentences.zh: 自惟虛薄，兢懼已深。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my emptiness and shallowness, my fear and trembling are already deep.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my emptiness, my fear is already deep.

sentences.zh: 若建承華，本歸皇胄；

translations.literal: If the Heir Apparent's establishment is built, it fundamentally returns to the imperial grandson;
translations.idiomatic: If the Heir Apparent is built, it returns to the imperial grandson;

sentences.zh: 心口相誓，惟擬晉安。

translations.literal: heart and mouth together swear—only Prince Jin'an is intended.
translations.idiomatic: heart and mouth swear—only Prince Jin'an is intended.

sentences.zh: 如或虛言，神明所殛。

translations.literal: If empty words, the spirits will destroy me.
translations.idiomatic: If empty words, the spirits will destroy me.

sentences.zh: 覽今所示，深遂本懷。

translations.literal: Reading what you now show, it deeply fulfills my original heart.
translations.idiomatic: Reading what you show, it fulfills my original heart.

sentences.zh: 戢慰之情，無寄言象。

translations.literal: The feeling of restraint and comfort has no words to carry it.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint and comfort have no words to carry them.

sentences.zh: 但公憂勞之重，旣稟齊恩；

translations.literal: But the weight of your anxious toil has already received Qi's grace;
translations.idiomatic: But your anxious toil has already received Qi's grace;

sentences.zh: 忠義之情，復及梁貳。

translations.literal: the feeling of loyalty and righteousness again reaches Liang's second rank.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty and righteousness again reach Liang's second rank.

sentences.zh: 華夷兆庶，豈不懷風？

translations.literal: The hundred surnames of China and barbarians—who does not turn to the wind?
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and barbarians—who does not turn to the wind?

sentences.zh: 宗廟明靈，豈不相感？

translations.literal: The temple's bright spirits—how would they not respond in feeling?
translations.idiomatic: The temple spirits—how would they not respond?

sentences.zh: 正爾迴斾，仍向歷陽。

translations.literal: Just now I turn the banners and still head for Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Just now I turn the banners and still head for Liyang.

sentences.zh: 所期質累，便望來彼。

translations.literal: The hostages expected—look to their coming there.
translations.idiomatic: The hostages expected—look to their coming there.

sentences.zh: 衆軍不渡，已著盟書。

translations.literal: The armies will not cross—this is already written in the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: The armies will not cross—this is already in the covenant.

sentences.zh: 斯則大齊聖主之恩規，上黨英王之然諾，得原失信，終不爲也。

translations.literal: This is Great Qi's sage ruler's gracious plan and the Prince of Shangdang's sworn promise—having obtained forgiveness for breach of faith, in the end he will not do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: This is Great Qi's gracious plan and Prince of Shangdang's sworn promise—having obtained forgiveness for breach, in the end he will not do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 惟遲相見，使在不賒。

translations.literal: I only await meeting you—may the envoy not delay.
translations.idiomatic: I only await meeting you—may the envoy not delay.

sentences.zh: 鄉國非遙，觸目號咽。

translations.literal: The homeland is not far—at every sight, wailing and sobbing."
translations.idiomatic: The homeland is not far—at every sight, wailing."

sentences.zh: 」僧辯使送質于鄴。

translations.literal: Sengbian sent the hostages to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian sent the hostages to Ye.

sentences.zh: 貞陽求渡衛士三千，僧辯慮其爲變，止受散卒千人而已，幷遣龍舟法駕往迎。

translations.literal: Zhenyang asked for three thousand guards to cross; Sengbian feared they would cause trouble and accepted only a thousand scattered troops; he also sent the dragon boat and imperial equipage to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyang asked for three thousand guards to cross; Sengbian feared trouble and accepted only a thousand scattered troops; he also sent the dragon boat and imperial equipage to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 貞陽濟江之日，僧辯擁檝中流，不敢就岸。

translations.literal: On the day Zhenyang crossed the river, Sengbian held the oars midstream and did not dare approach the shore.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyang crossed the river, Sengbian held the oars midstream and did not dare approach shore.

sentences.zh: 後乃同會于江寧浦。

translations.literal: Later they met together at Jiangning Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Later they met at Jiangning Ford.

sentences.zh: 貞陽旣踐偽位，仍授僧辯大司馬，領太子太傅、揚州牧，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: When Zhenyang had taken the false throne he still appointed Sengbian Grand Marshal, concurrently Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Governor of Yang Province; all else as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenyang took the false throne he appointed Sengbian Grand Marshal, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and Governor of Yang; all else unchanged.

sentences.zh: 陳霸先時爲司空、南徐州刺史，惡其飜覆，與諸將議，因自京口舉兵十萬，水陸俱至，襲于建康。

translations.literal: Chen Baxian was then Minister of Works and inspector of South Xu—he hated this reversal and discussed with the generals; from Jingkou he raised a hundred thousand men, coming by water and land together, and struck at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian was Minister of Works and inspector of South Xu—he hated the reversal and with the generals raised a hundred thousand men from Jingkou by water and land and struck Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 於是水軍到，僧辯常處於石頭城，是日正視事，軍人已逾城北而入，南門又馳白有兵來。

translations.literal: When the water army arrived, Sengbian was usually at Stone City; that day he was just handling affairs when soldiers had already crossed north of the city and entered; the southern gate also galloped word that troops were coming.
translations.idiomatic: When the fleet arrived, Sengbian was at Stone City handling affairs when soldiers crossed north of the city; the south gate also reported troops coming.

sentences.zh: 僧辯與其子頠遽走出閤，左右心腹尚數十人。

translations.literal: Sengbian and his son Wei hurried out of the pavilion; close retainers of heart and belly still numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian and his son Wei hurried from the pavilion; close retainers still numbered several tens.

sentences.zh: 衆軍悉至，僧辯計無所出，乃據南門樓乞命拜請。

translations.literal: When all the armies had arrived, Sengbian had no plan left; he then held the southern gate tower, begging for life and bowing in request.
translations.idiomatic: When all armies arrived, Sengbian had no plan; he held the south gate tower, begging life and bowing.

sentences.zh: 霸先因命縱火焚之，方共頠下就執。

translations.literal: Baxian thereupon ordered fire set to burn it; only then did he and Wei come down and be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian ordered fire set to burn it; only then he and Wei came down and were seized.

sentences.zh: 霸先曰：「我有何辜，公欲與齊師賜討？

translations.literal: Baxian said: "What crime have I, that you wished to grant Qi's army leave to come punish me?
translations.idiomatic: Baxian said, "What crime have I, that you wished to let Qi's army come punish me?

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「何意全無防備？

translations.literal: " He also said: "Why did you intend to have no defense at all?
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Why no defense at all?

sentences.zh: 」僧辯曰：「委公北門，何謂無備。

translations.literal: " Sengbian said: "I entrusted the north gate to you—how do you call that no defense?
translations.idiomatic: " Sengbian said, "I entrusted the north gate to you—how is that no defense?

sentences.zh: 」爾夜斬之。

translations.literal: " That night he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 長子髂，承聖初歷官至侍中。

translations.literal: The eldest son, Yi, in the early Manifest Fidelity era successively reached office up to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Yi in early Manifest Fidelity rose to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，僧辯平建業，遣霸先守京口，都無備防。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sengbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Baxian to guard Jingkou with no defensive preparations at all.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Baxian to guard Jingkou with no defenses.

sentences.zh: 髂屢以爲言，僧辯不聽，竟及於禍。

translations.literal: Yi repeatedly spoke of this; Sengbian would not listen, and in the end he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yi repeatedly warned him; Sengbian would not listen and met disaster.

sentences.zh: 西魏寇江陵，世祖遣髂督城內諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Western Wei raided Jiangling, Emperor Yuan sent Yi to supervise military affairs within the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei raided Jiangling, Yuan sent Yi to supervise military affairs in the city.

sentences.zh: 荊城陷，髂隨王琳入齊，爲竟陵郡守。

translations.literal: When Jing city fell, Yi followed Wang Lin into Qi and became magistrate of Jingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell, Yi followed Wang Lin into Qi and became magistrate of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 齊遣琳鎮壽春，將圖江左。

translations.literal: Qi sent Lin to garrison Shouyang, intending to take the left of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent Lin to garrison Shouyang, intending to take the Yangtze left bank.

sentences.zh: 及陳平淮南，執琳殺之。

translations.literal: When Chen pacified Huainan, they seized Lin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen pacified Huainan, they seized Lin and killed him.

sentences.zh: 髂聞琳死，乃出郡城南，登高冢上號哭，一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When Yi heard Lin was dead, he went south of the commandery city, climbed a high mound, and wailed; in one burst of grief he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi heard Lin was dead, he went south of the city, climbed a high mound, wailed once, and died.

sentences.zh: 髂弟頒，少有志節，恒隨從世祖。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Biao from youth had lofty resolve and always followed Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Biao from youth had lofty resolve and always followed Yuan.

sentences.zh: 及荊城陷覆，沒於西魏。

translations.literal: When Jing city was overrun he was lost in Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was overrun he was lost in Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自侯景寇逆，世祖據有上游，以全楚之兵委僧辯將率之任。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the time Hou Jing rebelled, Emperor Yuan held the upper reaches and entrusted the troops of all Chu to Sengbian's command.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From Hou Jing's rebellion, Yuan held the upper reaches and entrusted all Chu's troops to Sengbian.

sentences.zh: 及克平禍亂，功亦著焉，在乎策勳，當上臺之賞。

translations.literal: When he had crushed the calamity his merit too was manifest; in recording merit he ought to have received reward on the highest terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When he crushed the calamity his merit was manifest; in recording merit he ought to have received the highest reward.

sentences.zh: 敬帝以高祖貽厥之重，世祖繼體之尊，洎渚宮淪覆，理膺寶祚。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing bore the weight of Emperor Gaozu's legacy and Emperor Yuan's succession in the line; when Zhugong Palace was submerged, by right he should have received the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing bore Gaozu's legacy and Yuan's succession; when Zhugong fell, by right he should have received the throne.

sentences.zh: 僧辯位當將相，義存伊、霍，乃受脅齊師，傍立支庶。

translations.literal: Sengbian stood in the place of general and minister with the righteousness of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—yet he accepted coercion from Qi's army and set up a collateral scion at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian stood as general and minister with Yi Yin and Huo Guang's righteousness—yet he accepted Qi's coercion and set up a collateral scion.

sentences.zh: 苟欲行夫忠義，何忠義之遠矣？

translations.literal: If he wished to practice loyalty and righteousness, how far loyalty and righteousness had fled!
translations.idiomatic: If he wished loyalty and righteousness, how far they had fled!

sentences.zh: 樹國之道旣虧，謀身之計不足，自致殲滅，悲矣！

translations.literal: The way of establishing a state was already lost; the plan for preserving himself was insufficient—he brought on his own destruction. Lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: The way of establishing a state was lost; the plan for himself insufficient—he brought on his own destruction. Lamentable!

translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
